Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "Camera Repair Estimate 24-0718
Prepared July 18, 2024, for Mara Velez
Equipment: Fujifilm X-T4 body, serial number 1A23K04567

The camera was received at the Harbor Street service counter on July 16 with its body cap, one battery, and a short written note describing an intermittent shutter problem. The customer reported that the camera sometimes displayed “Shutter error” after several consecutive exposures, then worked again after the battery was removed and reinstalled. She said the issue had occurred during two indoor events and once outdoors, but she could not reproduce it reliably at the counter. The camera showed no visible impact damage, and the battery supplied with it held a normal charge during intake testing.

Initial inspection found light wear on the body edges and a small scuff beside the card door. The card door closes securely, both memory-card slots recognize test cards, and the rear display and electronic viewfinder show a stable image. The lens mount has no looseness, and the contacts are clean. The customer did not leave a lens, so the estimate covers testing with the shop’s reference lens only. No image files were copied or opened during the inspection; the two cards supplied by the customer were returned to her at intake.

The fault appeared during repeated testing with the shop battery and reference lens. After a sequence of thirty exposures at a moderate pace, the camera stopped responding to the shutter button and displayed the same error noted on the intake form. Removing and reinstalling the battery restored operation. A slower sequence did not reproduce the fault, and the camera did not show an error during a short video test. These results point to an intermittent shutter assembly problem, although the fault may not occur during every test cycle. The estimate therefore includes replacement of the shutter assembly and a final sequence test.

The proposed work is limited to the camera body. It includes removing the top and front covers, replacing the shutter assembly, checking the shutter flex connections, and reassembling the body with the original exterior parts. The technician will also clean the accessible sensor cover glass and inspect the card-slot contacts while the covers are removed. This is not a sensor replacement or a full exterior refurbishment. If inspection after disassembly reveals additional damage or a separate fault, the shop will stop and contact the customer with a revised estimate before doing work outside the items listed here.

1. Bench diagnostic and intake testing: $45.00
2. Shutter assembly, including parts handling: $286.00
3. Replacement labor and functional testing: $165.00
4. Return shipping, insured: $18.00
5. Estimated sales tax: $23.60

Estimated total: $537.60. This figure is based on the visible condition and tests completed so far. The diagnostic charge is included in the total, not added again after repair. The parts line covers one shutter assembly for this model; it does not include a new battery, memory card, lens, or camera strap. Return shipping is calculated for one body packed in the shop’s standard protective box. A different delivery address or shipping service could change that amount, and any change would be discussed before dispatch.

“Please tell me before replacing anything beyond the shutter,” Mara wrote on the intake form. That request is noted on the work order. The shop will seek authorization if the technician finds a second defect, if the specified part is unavailable, or if the work is likely to exceed the estimate. No additional repair is included unless the customer approves the revised amount. The estimate does not promise that the reported error will be eliminated in every shooting condition; the final test will check the repaired shutter through repeated still-image exposures and basic camera controls.

The shutter assembly is listed as available through the distributor at the time this estimate was prepared. Distributor availability can change before an order is placed, and the quoted part price is valid for 30 days. If the part cannot be obtained at that price, the shop will contact Mara before ordering an alternative or changing the estimate. The repair schedule begins when the estimate is approved and the required part is in hand; no completion date has been assigned yet. The body will remain in its padded storage tray while authorization and parts arrangements are pending.

The estimate does not include recovery of deleted images or transfer of files. The cards were handed back to Mara, and she is responsible for keeping them and any original image files. The camera will be returned with the same battery and body cap received at intake. The counter record also lists a black fabric strap, but it was not included with the equipment and is not held by the repair shop. Cosmetic scuffs noted during intake are recorded for identification and are not part of the proposed work.

This document is an estimate, not a completed repair receipt. It was prepared by Leon Park, service technician, and reviewed against the intake notes before being sent to Mara by email. The shop’s service counter is open Tuesday through Saturday, 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.; the repair bench is closed on Sundays and Mondays. Questions about the itemized work can be directed to the service desk using reference number 24-0718.
